Let's discuss the resistance-wire strain transducer type first.
Variable-resistance gages for measuring small changes in length are called resistance strain gages because of their early use in stress analysis.
One such device, a bonded-wire strain gage is shown below. This gage consists of a conducting material as a fine wire or a thin sheet cemented to the material to be stressed.
The thin sheet is usually made of carbon-like substance, this provides a resistance high enough that will make it convenient to obtain high resistance measurements.
A wire of a known resistance is used to demonstrate the principle of the device.
If the wire is stretched or compressed, the length of the wire increases and the cross-sectional area of the wire decreases. This increases the resistance of the wire.
The formula used to determine this relationship is R = L/A, or
Resistance = Wire Length / Wire Cross Section. gth Ohm symbol = Resistance
The elastic limit of the wire is not to be exceeded. The change of resistance to the change in length is a linear relationship.
This relationship translates into electrical signals, the change in resistance can be measured and the strain calculated.
Typical measurements might be of x-rays, cosmic rays, alpha, or beta particles.
Transducers made of these materials are self-generating; the electrical energy produced is linearly proportional to the energy of the measurand.

Another type of variable-inductance device is a differential transformer.
Generally, variable-inductance devices are used in frequency sensitive devices, particularly FM transmitters.
The ferromagnetic core is moved between primary transformer L1 and the two secondary transformers L2 and L3.
The ferromagnetic core is moved between primary transformer L1 and the two secondary transformers L2 and L3.
DEFINITION
FERROMAGNETIC - Materials that have magnetic properties similar to iron or iron alloy.
Moving the magnetic slug changes the magnetic coupling between the primary and secondary transformers.
Since L2 and L3 are in series, with the magnetic fields pointing toward each other the inductance from L1 is reduced.
If the ferrite slug is moved between transformer L1 and L2 the inductance between the two increases, and the inductance between L1 and L3 decreases.
This is known as permeability tuning, because the ferrite core has a higher degree of permeability between L1 and L2.
However, it has the opposite effect between L1 and L3. There is no longer an iron core between the two, but an air gap.
Since air has a lower permeability than iron, the inductance is less.
The output voltage is proportional to the mechanical displacement of the core.
If the ferrite slug is moved up or down the phase will either lead or lag the input current by a maximum of 90 degrees.
Generally, variable-inductance devices are used in frequency sensitive devices, particularly FM transmitters.
If L1 and L2 are aligned, the inductance between them will be _______ than the inductance between L1 and L3.
Since the permeability of iron is higher than air, the inductance will be higher between L1 and L2 and lower between L1 and L3.

The voltage applied to the potentiometer may be either alternating current or direct current.
Advantages of the potentiometer-type device are in its simplicity, high-level output, and ease with which it can be tapered.
Taper refers to the distribution of resistance along the resistive element.

Voltage-measuring devices encompass many different kinds of instruments.
Some examples are geiger counters, ionization chambers, and ionization pressures gages.
DEFINITION

IONIZATION - The formation of one or more ions by the addition of electrons to or removal of electrons from an electrically neutral atomic or molecular configuration by heat, electrical discharge, radiation, or chemical reaction.
Electronic transducers use motion, production, or control of free electrons. These include photoelectric, ionization, thermoelectric and piezoelectric transducers.
Any phenomenon that produces a variation in light intensity, position, or color may be measured/detected with photoelectric transducers.
These include photoconductor, photovoltaic, and photoemissive devices.
The term photoconductivity describes changes of conductivity induced by illumination in a gas, solid, or liquid medium.
Most photoconductive devices operate in series with a voltage source. Variations in conductivity produce a corresponding output voltage change.
Photovoltaic cells develop an internal EMF when illuminated by energy in the visible infrared and ultraviolet regions of the spectrum.
Commercially-available photovoltaic cells have outputs proportional to the area exposed to radiant energy.

Photoemissive transducers are of two general types: gas or high-vacuum diodes, and multiplier photocubes.
The electron-emitting element (cathode) in these tubes is coated with a photosensitive substance.
A positive voltage is applied to the electron collecting element (anodes).
Photoelectrons are emitted by the cathode and collected by the anode, producing current flow in the circuit.
Current flow depends on the wavelength and intensity of the light illuminating the cathode.
As the light on the photocathode varies, the current changes, causing a variation in the voltage drop across a load resistor in series with the tube.
Ionization transducers operate on the principle, that an atom ejects an orbital electron when a fast-moving charged particle approaches sufficiently close to it.
The residue of the atom is now a positively-charge ion, and the incident particles are ionizing radiations.
Nuclear radiations can be measured by observing the resulting ionization when they pass through a medium such as a gas.
Typical measurements might be of x-rays, cosmic rays, alpha, or beta particles.
Thermolectric transducers work on this principle: at the junction of the two dissimilar metals there exists an EMF that depends on temperature.
If the circuit is closed by another remote junction of two dissimilar metals, an opposing EMF exists at the other junction.
If the junctions are at the same temperature, the EMFs are equal and no current flows.
When one junction is at a higher temperature, the EMF at the hot junction exceeds the EMF at the cold junction, and current flow depends on the circuit resistance.
If two dissimilar metals are joined and the temperature is equal at the other junction, the EMFs are _______
Remember, if the junctions of the two dissimilar metals are at the same temperature, the EMFs are equal and no current flow.

Piezoelectric transducers work on the principle that certain materials can generate an electrical voltage when subjected to mechanical stress.
Much like a crystal record player cartridge, the record grooves provide stress to the stylus, causing it to vibrate through the crystal.
This piezoelectric property is common to natural crystals such as quartz and tourmaline, synthetic materials such as Rochelle salts, and ceramics such as barium titanate.
Transducers made of these materials are self-generating; the electrical energy produced is linearly proportional to the energy of the measurand.
Crystals when _______ stressed, can generate an electrical voltage.
Remember the crystal record player cartridge, the grooves in the record stress the stylus, causing it to vibrate. These vibrations are then transmitted through the crystal.

DISCUSSION

An obvious example of transducers is the conversion of sound to electrical energy. But most often transducers convert mechanical motion to electrical energy to provide monitoring of the movement, position, temperature, or other physical condition of a device or application.
